prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1035; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A dated inspection photo shows the same dent before this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: The claim was reported by phone the same day as the side impact at the intersection, and the claimant described the crash as the other car entering on the passenger side. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer and said they would handle the paperwork directly.

Entry 2: Police attended and confirmed the claimant was in the vehicle at the time, and the responding officer's notes match the account given to us. The policyholder was not driving, but the driver lives in the same household and is covered as a household member.

Entry 3: Photos taken at the scene confirm the point of impact and the general position of both vehicles, though no independent witnesses have come forward. The damage to the claimant's vehicle appears mostly consistent with the described impact.

Entry 4: The claimant reported a knee injury and attended urgent care the following day, where the findings were recorded in line with the force of a side impact. No earlier injury to the same area is known from the claimant's records so far.

Entry 5: An inspection photo on file, taken before this crash, shows the same dent on the rear door, so the damage is not entirely new. Nothing we have reviewed suggests the damage occurred before the coverage started.

Entry 6: The claimant has given the same account of the collision in each conversation, including the phone call, the recorded statement, and the follow-up call. Treatment has followed a usual course, with physiotherapy sessions tapering off as the knee improved.

Entry 7: Based on the photos, police record, medical notes, and the consistent account, the claim is being assessed for payment under the policy. The file will be sent to the handler for final review, with the inspection photo and the prior dent noted for the record.
